# Agentic AI workflows for research

::: {.lead}
Understand how AI works. Put it to use in your research. Keep consequential judgment in human hands, and examine the institutions that govern the technology.
:::

[Explore the course](course.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

Working course materials. Introduction plus five core sections; the fifth section is still being developed.
:::

## A workflow you can inspect

The course connects technical foundations to a research system you can direct, verify, and improve. You will build a workspace, define the decisions that remain yours, and apply an agent to a bounded task you actually need.

Governance extends beyond your own desk. We will examine control over data, institutional responsibilities, and the societal consequences of delegation.

## Learning through application

Each core section is planned around supporting materials, a two-hour live call, and a practice exercise. Exercises build on your existing workspace and produce evidence of what you have done.

The final project brings the pipeline together: source data, manage questions, merge and analyze, then explain the results through a website.

[Read the course sequence](course.qmd) · [See the final-project brief](project.qmd)

## Evidence and disagreement

The course draws on [With Great Powers](https://simonepaciphd.github.io/with-great-powers/) and the [Working with AI Agents guide](https://simonepaciphd.github.io/ai-os-public/).

Students can challenge the instructor's position. The aim is careful reasoning supported by evidence, with uncertainty and competing arguments kept visible.
